PullRequest.Title: Changing the wording of the problem status bar indicator

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restoration initializes the limit indicator contribution and its diagnostic status metadata.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At LifecyclePhase.Restored, the contribution constructs three accessors and three LanguageStatusEntry objects; the changed diagnostic name, label, and source strings are localized once during accessor construction. This synchronous constant-size work must complete during contribution initialization, but the diff does not add any operation or change call count.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed at one DiagnosticDecorationAccessor and three changed constant strings per contribution instance; it does not scale with files, diagnostics, editors, or workspaces.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous initialization on the workbench lifecycle path; no queue, limiter, mutex, or concurrent fan-out is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Built localization may read the existing in-memory NLS message table; development uses the fallback literal. Cold and warm behavior and cache keys are unchanged because localization keys and call sites are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete diff and constructor trace that no repeated, eager heavyweight, retained, or boundary work was introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the replacement literals differ only slightly in byte length, and cardinality remains fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR replaces constant wording without changing initialization frequency, allocation shape beyond negligible fixed string size, or downstream behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: A marker source or editor decoration count crosses a limit and updates the active editor's Problems language-status warning.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Marker-limit change synchronously calls DiagnosticDecorationLimitReporter._update, formats one detail string only when a limit exists, fires only when the resulting limited state changes, then disposes/registers one language status. The changed wording stays on the same path and adds no await or expensive boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active editor and one status entry per state transition. Diagnostic count can exceed 5,000, but only the numeric limit is interpolated; message construction does not iterate over diagnostics and the effective status cardinality remains one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event handling for the active editor. Background-editor marker changes are ignored by the active LanguageStatusEntry listener, and identical over-limit states are coalesced by the limited-string equality check.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. The localized format uses the existing in-memory NLS lookup, and an unchanged limited string suppresses repeat status recreation; cold and warm behavior are identical before and after the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing marker-limit events through _update, _getLimitedMessage, LanguageStatusEntry.updateStatusItem, and LanguageStatusServiceImpl.addStatus.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact status-bar rendering cost is not measured, but the diff neither changes rendering frequency nor adds layout/DOM work; only bounded text content changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Constant wording changes neither fan out per diagnostic nor increase event, localization, registration, or rendering frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: The user switches active editors while a diagnostic limit warning is present.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The active-editor event disposes the previous listener/status, reads the selected editor's limit reporter, and registers at most one warning. The changed accessor strings are reused and the detail string follows the existing formatting path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected editor and at most one diagnostic status per switch; background diagnostics do not multiply work on this path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Editor switches are processed synchronously and serially by the event source; prior listener ownership is disposed before the new listener is installed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or miss behavior. Accessor metadata remains retained for the contribution lifetime exactly as before, and status lifetime remains bounded by editor selection and contribution disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the active-editor handler, disposal path, and tests demonstrating background changes do not recreate the active warning.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No material uncertainty: changed strings do not alter listener count, lifecycle, or status cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff does not affect cleanup, concurrency, retained state, or per-switch work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full one-file, two-hunk diff. Traced initialization, diagnostic-limit updates, language-status registration, active-editor switching, localization, rendering reachability, lifecycle, cardinality, cache behavior, and external boundaries. All changes are bounded replacement strings with unchanged keys, control flow, frequency, concurrency, and resource lifetime; no actionable performance issue or regression-fix signal was found.
